notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix (none found). §1985:VII.2.2.2 prints the paragraph as the header and '{ file-control-entry }' with an ellipsis: one entry at least, then as many as wanted (§1985:IV.2.1.4: 'When braces, { } , enclose a portion of a general format, one of the options contained within the braces must be either explicitly specified or implicitly selected.'). Implemented at 85: fileControlParagraph parses FILE-CONTROL, its period and any number of fileControlClauseGroup entries, and BindFileControl binds each (the witness declares two files and reads both back). Not implemented: the lower bound. fileControlParagraph writes fileControlClauseGroup* with no edition arm and BindFileControl iterates whatever entries there are, so the 2023 form (§2023:12.4.4.2, entries in brackets) is accepted at every edition: at --std 85 a FILE-CONTROL paragraph with no entry compiles and runs, alone and before an I-O-CONTROL paragraph. The slice-04 record of 1985-FMT-IV.6.2.3.1 reports the same acceptance from the Environment Division format (with the INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION that has no FILE-CONTROL paragraph, which is that row's and not this one's).

next.reason: 1985: "FILE-CONTROL. { file-control-entry } …"; 2023: "FILE-CONTROL. [ file-control-entry ] …". 1985 braces require at least one file-control-entry. The 2023 brackets make it optional, so a FILE-CONTROL paragraph with no entries is now accepted.
